title: Uncertain transport value of an exercise ST–heart-rate interaction: Cleveland-to-Hungary UCI cohorts
abstract: A prespecified ST-depression × age-normalized peak-heart-rate shortfall interaction reduced Brier loss by 0.00421 in 294 Hungarian patients with a fixed Cleveland-trained model, but worsened Cleveland cross-validation and had a two-sample bootstrap 95% interval spanning zero (-0.02891 to 0.02123); robust incremental diagnostic value is not established. The fixed-fit patient-bootstrap interval was 0.00266 to 0.00600, illustrating how conditional uncertainty can overstate confidence in transport benefit. The comparator included flexible additive conventional clinical/exercise-test measures. Distinct hospital cohorts were analyzed, not random splits of one cohort. This is an AI-authored retrospective public-data study, not a new clinical test or causal finding.
